title: Simulasi TOEFL ITP Bagian 2 & Estimasi Skor

lesson.intro: Bagian kedua simulasi ini berisi reading, lalu langkah membaca hasil. Semua soal ditulis sendiri untuk latihan dan bukan soal resmi. Estimasi skor di sini hanya perkiraan dari latihan.

sections.heading: Refleksi setelah tes
sections.bodyMd: Setelah tes, tulis **reflection** singkat. Cari satu **strength** dan satu **weakness**. Jangan hanya melihat angka akhirnya.

sections.heading: Target dan peta jalan
sections.bodyMd: Tetapkan **target** yang realistis. Lalu buat **roadmap** dengan **milestone** kecil, misalnya menyelesaikan satu set bacaan setiap dua hari.

sections.heading: Masa mandek dan momentum
sections.bodyMd: Saat mencapai **plateau**, ubah satu bagian dari metodemu. **Momentum** tumbuh ketika kamu melihat kemajuan kecil dari waktu ke waktu. Catat latihanmu agar kemajuannya terlihat.

block3.title: Membaca Hasil dan Menyusun Langkah
block3.text:
After a full practice simulation, the most useful step is reflection. Many students look only at the final number, but a score report contains more information. It shows your strength in areas such as reading comprehension, and it also reveals your weakness in others. A clear picture of both helps you plan the next stage of study.

A readiness check should begin with your target. If your goal is a score that matches a university requirement, write that target down and compare it with your current level. The gap between the two is your roadmap. Break the roadmap into milestones, such as finishing one reading set every two days or adding fifty words to your vocabulary each week.

Progress does not always move in a straight line. Many learners reach a plateau, a period when their scores stop rising for several weeks. This is normal. During a plateau, the best approach is to change one part of your method, such as practicing with shorter passages or reviewing mistakes more carefully. Small changes can restart the momentum.

Momentum is the feeling that your effort is producing results. It grows when you finish tasks on time and see improvement in your notes. Keep a simple record of your practice sessions. Over time, the record becomes evidence that your work is paying off.

A transition to a new exam format is also a natural next step. Skills from one test often carry over to another, but each format has its own rules. Before moving on, check that your strengths can support your weaker areas. Only then should you take the next challenge.
